<reflection>
After two experiments, M7 remains the best-fitting model, but the NLL differences among the top candidates are still very small (ΔNLL < 0.3). The second experiment with high substrate concentration (5.0 M) did not dramatically separate the models, suggesting that substrate inhibition (M7) and various deactivation mechanisms (M16, M11, M17, etc.) all fit the data similarly under the conditions tested. The aim of the second turn was to discriminate using high [S], which provided some separation but not enough. We need a new experiment that targets mechanistic differences more effectively.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
The leading candidates include M7 (substrate inhibition via ternary complex), M16 (deactivation by S + catS), M11 (deactivation by S + cat), M17 (deactivation by P + catS), and others. A key distinction is the role of product in deactivation: M17 explicitly involves product in the deactivation step, while others do not. Introducing initial product should differentially affect these mechanisms. 

- **Hypothesis discrimination**: The critical difference is whether deactivation is accelerated by the presence of product (M17) or not (others). Additionally, reversible product inhibition (present in most mechanisms) will reduce the initial rate, but M17 will show an extra slowdown due to immediate deactivation.

- **Discriminative experiment design**: Use the same substrate and catalyst concentrations as the first experiment (1.0 M S, 0.01 M cat) but add initial product at 0.2 M. This amount is significant enough to observe effects but not so high as to dominate the kinetics entirely. This condition directly tests product-dependent deactivation and reversible inhibition.

- **Contrastive predictions**:
  - **M17 (deactivation by P + catS)**: Initial product will cause immediate deactivation, leading to a substantially lower initial rate than predicted by reversible inhibition alone. The time course will show rapid early flattening, with less total product formed over time compared to the no-product case.
  - **M7 (substrate inhibition)**: Initial product may bind to catS to form catS2 (via reverse of the last step), potentially increasing the inhibited complex. This could reduce the initial rate, but the curvature should remain similar to the no-product case, without extra deactivation-driven flattening.
  - **M1/M2 (simple reversible)**: Initial product will lower the initial rate due to reversible product inhibition, but the time course will approach the same equilibrium conversion as without product (just shifted kinetics). No extra deactivation.
  - **M11/M16/M14 (deactivation independent of product)**: These will show reversible inhibition lowering the initial rate, but the deactivation pattern (if any) will be similar to the no-product run because deactivation depends only on S or catS. The time course may resemble that of run1 but scaled down.
</hypothesis>
